titles.title: SeriousSamFirstEncounter
titles.engine: Croteam Serious Engine 1, retail v1.00, OpenGL only. Bin\Engine.dll is 1,560,576 B, md5 6281c69ec427b9a0dd828bc1cbf0b14b, PE timestamp 0x3a9d4916 (2001-02-28). SeriousSam.exe is 425,984 B with PE subsystem 4.0. Its log prints 'Serious Sam version: v1.00'.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen OpenGL on the XP LCD boxes. All three launchers call FLEETRES.BAT and then rewrite Scripts\Game_startup.ini with sam_bFullScreen=1, sam_iScreenSizeI/J=%FR_W%/%FR_H% and gfx_iRefreshRate=%FR_HZ% (lines 54-61 of 'Play Serious Sam - The First Encounter.bat'). The GAMERES 'ssam' rule writes the same file at sync. The staged TFE Game_startup.ini holds only two comment lines, so overwriting it loses nothing. The .240 log shows 'CDS: mode set to 1920x1080x0' on a RADEON X800. Exception, .195 (Windows 7): every mode returns DISP_CHANGE_BADMODE, including the four 640x480 recovery modes, and the engine exits with FatalError. Disassembly suggests a cheaper cause than the one the survey gave. TFE 1.00 and TSE 1.05 share a byte-identical CDS set-mode routine (Engine.dll 0x600faedd and 0x6003ad1d). The only difference is the refresh variable. TFE reads gfx_iRefreshRate, which the launcher sets to 60, so TFE adds DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY=60 on top of DM_DISPLAYFLAGS=4. TSE ignores that line as undeclared, and TSE sets 1920x1080 on the same .195 box. The refresh line is therefore the prime suspect. This is unproven until tested on .195.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table filtered by the driver. Engine.dll holds _areResolutions at file offset 0x159200: 22 int32 w,h pairs from 320x240 to 856x480. The entry count is stored as data at 0x1592b0 (value 22). The loop at 0x600fad99 tests each entry with ChangeDisplaySettingsA(dm, CDS_TEST|CDS_FULLSCREEN = 6) and adds the modes that pass to the list at 0x6022e240. SeriousSam.exe imports ?EnumDisplayModes@CGfxLibrary@@QBEAAVCListHead@@XZ, which returns that list, and the fullscreen RESOLUTION trigger shows it. The table has no 16:9 entry except 848x480/856x480 NTSC. IsWideScreen is exactly 856x480 (0x600fc1e0). IsDualHead is w*3==h*8 (0x600fc1c0). When the current mode is not in the list, the trigger shows 640x480, and pressing APPLY from that screen would set it. The TFE binary was not run on hardware in this review. The identical menu code in TSE was run on .123 (see that title): it lists 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x960, 1280x1024 and 848x480, and it opens showing 640x480 while the game runs at 1920x1080.

The hardware run of the identical menu code in TSE on .123 is 123-tse-SHEET-opengl-resolution-cycle.png and 123-tse-05-videooptions.png. Survey: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/static-serious-engine-tables.txt; {123,145,195,240}/SeriousSamFirstEncounter__Scripts_Game_startup.ini (1920/1080/60); 195/SeriousSamFirstEncounter__SeriousSam.log (BADMODE for all five tries, FatalError); 240/SeriousSamFirstEncounter__SeriousSam.log (mode set to 1920x1080). TSE 1.07 was checked as a possible upgrade source: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Game Updates/serious-sam-tse-1.07.exe has the same 23-entry table at Engine.dll 0x1dd8e0, and its SeriousSam.exe carries stxt774, stxt371 and BoG_.
titles.fix: (1) Menu: a data-only, same-size patch of the staged Bin\Engine.dll. Overwrite the three Matrox dual-head pairs: 0x159288 (1280,480) becomes (1280,720); 0x159290 (1600,600) becomes (1600,900); 0x159298 (2048,768) becomes (1920,1080). Leave the count at 0x1592b0 at 22. None of the new pairs trips IsDualHead or IsWideScreen, both verified above. (2) .195: before any version change, A/B test one launch there. Write the startup script without the gfx_iRefreshRate line, or with gfx_iRefreshRate=0, and delete sam_iDriver=1 from that box's hand-written Scripts\PersistentSymbols.ini, which selects the absent '3Dfx' adapter. If it still returns BADMODE, add sam_iDisplayDepth=2 (explicit 32-bit). Only if both fail, consider the TFE 1.05 patch, which breaks joins to the v1.00 server. (3) Optional: add 'sam_bFirstStarted=0;' to what the launcher and GAMERES write. The 'SeriousSam is starting for the first time' modal otherwise blocks every start on a box where the game has never exited cleanly. The log shows Game_startup.ini runs before that check. The modal was observed on .123 for TSE, and the .240 TFE log shows the same message.
titles.fix_source: Already in tree: an in-place same-size edit of /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SeriousSamFirstEncounter/Bin/Engine.dll. The .195 test changes only the startup script written by scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (ssam_startup_ini), provisioning/discmount/specs/SeriousSamFirstEncounter-{Play,Host,Join}.json and agent/shared/gameres.h (the 'ssam' body). The TFE 1.05 fallback is /mnt/retro-share/Files/Game Updates/serious-sam-tfe-1.05.zip.
titles.fix_risk: Low for the table edit. Only the menu enumeration reads the table, and the runtime mode set does not. Multiplayer is expected to be unaffected: Engine.dll is loaded by LoadLibrary, not through the engine's CRC-checked file system, and the host server has its own copy. Still prove a join to 192.168.1.132:25600 afterwards. The edit keeps the file size, so publish through gvfs and verify the md5 through /mnt. An smbclient 2007 timestamp would let GAMESYNC skip it. Dropping the refresh line fleet-wide would cost the CRT boxes their explicit refresh, so limit it to .195/Win7 unless the test shows a reason to go wider. The refresh line is shared with TSE, which runs on .195 today only because TSE ignores it.
titles.hw_check: Use .145, .240 or .123. .123 now has DAEMON Tools, and XP GDI captures this engine fullscreen, as proven on .123 with TSE. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SeriousSamFirstEncounter" "Play Serious Sam - The First Encounter.bat". If an 'Information' #32770 window appears in WINLIST, send UIKEY RETURN; it is the first-run modal and it blocks the start. Wait for the window titled 'Serious Sam (FullScreen 1920x1080)'. The menu is keyboard-navigable. From SINGLE PLAYER, press DOWN x6 to OPTIONS, RETURN, RETURN (VIDEO OPTIONS), DOWN x3 to RESOLUTION, then RIGHT repeatedly, taking a SCREENSHOT at each step. Expected today: it opens at 640x480 and cycles through the driver-accepted table entries only, with no 1920x1080. After the patch, 1920x1080 is present. Never press APPLY. Leave with ESCAPE, run taskkill /f /im "SeriousSam.exe", then delete the Players\Player0-7.plr, Controls\Controls0-7.ctl and SeriousSam.log that the engine creates on a first run. For .195, run the refresh A/B test above and DOWNLOAD SeriousSam.log to check for 'CDS: mode set to 1920x1080'.
titles.verifier_notes: Menu claim CONFIRMED statically. The same menu code was then exercised on hardware through TSE on .123. Changed: (a) the .195 failure has a more specific suspect than 'TFE 1.00 has no working display path on Win7'. The two engines' CDS set-mode code is byte-identical except the refresh variable, and only TFE consumes the launcher's gfx_iRefreshRate=60. So the recommended first step is a one-launch test, not the 1.05 upgrade, which would break the v1.00 server join. (b) The table count is a data word at 0x1592b0, not a compiled immediate; replacing entries is still correct. (c) New side finding: the first-run 'starting for the first time' modal blocks unattended starts on every box where the game never exited cleanly. .195 avoids it only through its hand-written sam_bFirstStarted=0. The survey's .240, .123 and sam_iDriver notes are confirmed.

titles.title: SeriousSamSecondEncounter
titles.engine: Croteam Serious Engine 1, retail v1.05. Bin\Engine.dll is 1,929,274 B, md5 230c1b52f3bd125dc9af049b70472100, PE timestamp 0x3c172f28 (2001-12-12). It has OpenGL and Direct3D 8 renderers and runs GameMP via ModEXT.txt. The 1.07 patch on the share wraps SeriousSam.exe in SafeDisc (stxt774, stxt371, BoG_ confirmed in this review) and keeps the same 23-entry table.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen, confirmed on hardware this session. On .123 the window was 'Serious Sam (FullScreen 1920x1080)' and the log shows 'CDS: mode set to 1920x1080x0' on an ATI Radeon HD 3850 AGP under OpenGL. The mechanism is present but DEFECTIVE, and this is now proven on hardware. Both writers replace the whole of Scripts\Game_startup.ini: the launcher with '> ...Game_startup.ini', GAMERES with GR_OP_CFG. That drops TSE's four shipped lines, so the exe's compiled-in TFE defaults apply. On .123, SINGLE PLAYER > NEW GAME > NORMAL stayed on the difficulty screen, and the log reads "Starting session: 'Levels\01_Hatshepsut.wld' ... Cannot start game: Cannot open file ... 01_Hatshepsut.wld". The menu background fails the same way on Levels\Intro.wld. The TSE single-player campaign cannot start on any box whose startup script has been rewritten, which is all four LCD boxes. A third loss, found statically: sam_strGameName defaults to 'serioussam' (initialiser at 0x422b40), and 0x424307 copies it into _pNetwork at startup. The fleet's TSE server reports gamename 'serioussamse' (scripts/gameindex/sync.py), so the TSE LAN/GameSpy browser is likely matching TFE's name. That effect is unverified. gfx_iRefreshRate is undeclared in TSE (log line 85 on .123), so no refresh is requested.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table in Engine.dll at 0x1ad6d0: 23 pairs, 320x240 to 856x480, including 720x576. The OpenGL loop at 0x6003a8a1 runs CDS_TEST per entry. The Direct3D 8 loop at 0x6003ab16 keeps an EnumAdapterModes mode only if it equals a table entry with format 0x15-0x19 and passes CheckDeviceType. Both loops end at 0x601ad788. On .123 the observed RESOLUTION list is the same under OpenGL and under Direct3D: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 848x480, then it wraps. It opens showing 640x480 while running at 1920x1080 (SizeToResolution fallback), so APPLY from that screen would drop to 640x480.

titles.fix: (1) MUST-FIX, independent of resolution: stop destroying TSE's startup script. Either both writers re-emit the four shipped lines (sam_strFirstLevel, sam_strIntroLevel, sam_strTechTestLevel, sam_strGameName="serioussamse"), or stage Game_startup.ini as shipped plus a final 'include "Scripts\\FleetRes.ini";' and have both writers produce only FleetRes.ini. The engine itself runs Game_startup.ini through 'include', so that form is valid syntax. Update the ssam block in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py, provisioning/discmount/specs/SeriousSamSecondEncounter-{Play,Host,Join}.json (regenerate with make-mount-launcher.py), agent/shared/gameres.h and their mirror tests. (2) Do NOT switch TSE to gap_iRefreshRate as the survey proposed until it is tested on .195. The TFE-on-.195 evidence suggests an explicit refresh may be what makes this CDS code return BADMODE on Windows 7, and TSE works on .195 today because its refresh line is ignored. Simply omitting the refresh line for TSE is the safe choice. (3) Menu: the same-size Engine.dll patch. 0x1ad760 (1280,480) becomes (1280,720); 0x1ad768 (1600,600) becomes (1600,900); 0x1ad770 (2048,768) becomes (1920,1080). This covers OpenGL and Direct3D. (4) Optional: add sam_bFirstStarted=0; to the startup script. The first-run modal blocked the .123 start until RETURN was sent. (5) Do not use 1.07: it adds SafeDisc and keeps the same table.

It restores the campaign, and probably the TSE browser game name. (2) Adding a refresh value could break TSE on Windows 7, hence 'omit'. (3) Low, same reasoning as TFE: prove a join to 192.168.1.132:25610, run a two-box LAN game, and publish the same-size file through gvfs, verified via /mnt.

If WINLIST shows an 'Information' #32770 window, send UIKEY RETURN. The launcher left the TSE disc mounted in DAEMON Tools, which is the normal state after playing TSE.

titles.title: Shogo
titles.engine: LithTech 1.0 (Shogo 2.2). Client.exe (1999-03-05) runs with the -rez chain; the renderers are d3d.ren (305,152 B, md5 072bc370...) and soft.ren. CShell.dll v3 was carved from SHOGOP3.REZ at 0x2bca8: 525,824 B, md5 eb0286632a78bd488bd0f41f37114c4d.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen at 16 bpp, CONFIRMED on .123 this session. Both launchers write screenwidth and screenheight into autoexec.cfg through FLEETRES -setline, and GAMERES mirrors them. While running on .123 (Radeon HD 3850, XP), DISPLAYCFG read 1920x1080 at 16 bpp and 60 Hz, WINLIST showed the LithTech window at 0,0-1920x1080, and the main menu rendered fullscreen. So a 16-bpp 1080p mode also exists on an ATI box, not only on .145. The fallback 'Play Shogo.bat' (Shogo.exe) path remains unverified.
titles.menu_source: The list is enumerated from the driver, 16-bpp modes only: d3d.ren's EnumDisplayModes callback keeps dwRGBBitCount == 16. It is stored in a broken fixed table, and hardware REFUTES the survey's 'yes'. CShell v3 keeps 12 resolution slots per device, since each device record (stride 0x1cc) holds a 0x10c header plus 12 entries of 16 bytes. Entries are appended at 0x10003546 with NO bound check. The observed order is ASCENDING, not largest-first as the survey assumed. On .123 d3d.ren shows two devices. On the default '(d3d.ren) ATI Radeon HD 3850 AGP' device the RESOLUTION control cycles 640x480, 720x480, 800x600, 848x480, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x720, 1280x768, 1280x800, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1360x768, then '1835627088 x 544830049', '1986622020 x 29285' and '0 x 0', then wraps. Those three are the next device's description string read as numbers: 'Prim', 'ary ', 'Driv', 'er'. 1440x900, 1680x1050 and 1920x1080 are lost. On the second device, whose name shows as '(d3d.ren) Primary X' because the overflow corrupted it, all 15 driver modes appear, including 1920 x 1080. The DISPLAY MODE screen opens at '640 x 480' while the game runs at 1920x1080. soft.ren has two devices as well. Every LCD box enumerates more than 12 modes (15 on .123, 16 on .145, 20 on .195, 24 on .240), so the default device is truncated on all of them. The menu is keyboard-navigable (DOWN, RETURN, LEFT/RIGHT work). Roughly half of the GDI frames show the background without menu text.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/review-ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. 123-shogo-01-after-launch.png (1920x1080 main menu); 123-shogo-05-display-1.png (DISPLAY OPTIONS: '(d3d.ren) ATI Radeon HD 3850 AGP / 1920 x 1080'); 123-shogo-06-changemode-2.png (DISPLAY MODE opens at 640 x 480); 123-shogo-SHEET-ati-device-resolution-cycle.png and 123-shogo-08-res-*.png (12 real entries, then garbage); 123-shogo-SHEET-renderer-device-cycle.png (d3d.ren and soft.ren, two devices each); 123-shogo-SHEET-primary-device-resolution-cycle.png and 123-shogo-10-primaryres-10.png ('Primary X / 1920 x 1080'); 123-shogo-11-after-exit.png (desktop restored). static-review-disasm.txt has the unbounded append and the record layout. The per-box driver lists are in ../ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/{box}/gameres.json.
titles.fix: Two parts. Without a fix, 1080p is reachable only by switching 'renderer' to the corrupted '(d3d.ren) Primary X' device, and applying that selection is untested: the damaged name may not match any DirectDraw device. Preferred fix: a same-size patch of CShell.dll v3 inside SHOGOP3.REZ, file offset 0x2bca8 plus the DLL's own offsets. Detour the append at 0x10003546 to a code cave. CShell .text has 0xEB bytes of slack, since VirtualSize is 0x69315 and raw size is 0x69400. In the cave: when a device's count reaches 12, shift entries 1..11 down one slot (16 B each) and set count=11, then append as before. Each device then keeps its 12 LARGEST modes, 1920x1080 becomes the default device's last entry, and the overflow that writes garbage into the next device record stops. An alternative that leaves the vendor archive alone: ship the patched CShell.dll in a new REZ appended last to both launchers' -rez chains, since last-wins. Filtering modes in d3d.ren's callback was considered and rejected, because the per-box mode counts (15-24) make any single width filter fragile.
titles.fix_source: Already in tree: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Shogo/SHOGOP3.REZ, with CShell.dll at 0x2bca8 (525,824 B). Nothing needs downloading.
titles.fix_risk: Medium-high: a hand-written code patch in a 1999 DLL inside a REZ archive. CShell is client-side UI only. The host's shogo-server and the protocol are untouched, and the 'shell DLL version' check reads a constant this patch does not change. Prove it with the menu cycle below plus one mode APPLY. It is a same-size edit, so publish through gvfs and verify through /mnt. The two-box multiplayer join is already 'needs_human' in the DB.
titles.hw_check: Proven procedure on .123. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Shogo" "Play Shogo - direct engine.bat" and wait 25 s. Then UIKEY DOWN, DOWN, RETURN (options); RETURN (display); RETURN (change mode); DOWN (resolution); then RIGHT xN. Take up to 5 SCREENSHOTs per step and keep the frame whose max brightness exceeds 200, because the menu text flickers. Pass: '1920 x 1080' appears on the default '(d3d.ren) <card>' device and no numeric garbage appears. Also UP to renderer and RIGHT to confirm the device names are no longer corrupted. Do not press 'back' with a garbage entry selected. Exit with taskkill /f /im "Client.exe", then check DISPLAYCFG get and the autoexec.cfg md5 (both unchanged on .123 today: 1920x1080x32, cc723dba97e5887211101c6ca2cb6bc1).
titles.verifier_notes: REFUTED on hardware. The survey's 'yes' assumed a largest-first order and a harmless spill into unused device slots. Observed on .123: ascending order, the default device truncated at 12 with three garbage entries decoded from the next device's name, and 1920x1080 only under a second device whose own name is corrupted. The 16-bpp caveat is resolved for .123, where 1920x1080x16 was active. Cleanup: the game was killed without applying anything; autoexec.cfg content is unchanged (the launcher rewrote identical bytes, so only its mtime moved); no files were created; the desktop is 1920x1080x32.

titles.title: Turok2
titles.engine: Acclaim/Iguana Turok 2 engine, 1998 PC retail. The Direct3D renderer is Video_D3D.dll: 278,528 B, md5 b3919d01613a234a485fef78c2999fc6, PE timestamp 0x36b73374 (1999-02-02). Single player is Turok2English.exe, which needs the Turok 2 CD; the share has no image of it. Multiplayer is Turok2MPEnglish.exe, with no CD check.
titles.launch_sets: 1024x768 fullscreen, 32-bit. All three launchers compute T2SEL from FR_W43 (1280 on these panels, so 1024) and set only 1024^x^768 to 1 in Data\config.ned. The GAMERES rule is WRONG, confirmed: %SEL43:WxH% compares against t->w43/h43 by exact string match, and on the LCDs the 4:3 target is 1280x960, which Turok's list lacks. The rule therefore writes all six booleans to 0, as the deployed config.ned on .123, .145, .195 and .240 shows. .133 has the same problem, because its 4:3 target is also 1280x960. In the renderer, each mode boolean applies only when it equals 1 (ebx=1 at 0x100014f6). The width/height globals 0x1001fd84/0x1001fd94 are 0 in .data. The only fallback to 640x480 (0x1000264d) fires when a SELECTED mode is unavailable, never when none is selected. So a start that bypasses the launcher gets no mode; what the engine then does is unobserved.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded 6-entry list compiled into Video_D3D.dll: 320x240, 512x384, 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768 and 1280x1024 (records at 0x1001b030, stride 0x44). The DirectDraw enumeration callback at 0x1000223a marks a record available only on an exact width and height match. The 'Direct3D Properties' dialog (RT_DIALOG 102: 'Video Card', 'Resolution', 'Windowed' ...) fills its Resolution combobox from those records. The MP exe's 'Video' dialog (RT_DIALOG 131, 'Choose a Driver', 'Properties') opens it, reached from VIDEO in single.mnu/multi.mnu. On these LCDs the highest entry is 1280 x 1024. There is no custom mode.
titles.evidence: Survey: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/static-turok2-video_d3d.txt; {123,145,195,240}/Turok2__Data_config.ned (all six mode keys 0). Re-verified in this review: the dialog resources of Video_D3D.dll and Turok2MPEnglish.exe; the boolean-apply code at 0x10001647-0x100016f3 with ebx=1; the fallback at 0x100025fb-0x1000267f; the patch-site bytes (0x1b3a4 '1280 x 1024', 0x22c2 817e0c00050000, 0x16de c70584fd011000050000, 0x16e8 a394fd0110, 0x22cb 394e08); and .text slack of 0xF03 bytes. agent/shared/gameres.h lines 808-814, gr_expand SEL43, and tests/native/test_gameres.c:301-306. Compat DB: the 2026-08-31 10:50-10:53 rows claim 1920x1080 on .123, .240 and .246 for 'Play Turok 2.bat'.
titles.fix: (1) Required: make GAMERES pick the largest Turok entry that fits the 4:3 target, mirroring the launcher's T2SEL ladder: 1024 when W43 >= 1024, 800 when W43 >= 800, else 640. That needs a new token, e.g. %SELFIT43:1024x768% with the ladder 640/800/1024, plus updates to test_gameres.c and test_gameres_mirror.py. This stops the rule zeroing every mode on the four LCD boxes and .133. (2) The only route to an in-game 1920x1080 is a code patch of Video_D3D.dll that repurposes the 5:4 record. Change the label at 0x1b3a4 to '1920 x 1080' (same 11 bytes; this also renames the config.ned key). Change the width immediates at 0x22c5 and 0x16e4 from 0x500 to 0x780. Both heights reuse a register holding 0x400: 'cmp [esi+8],ecx' at 0x22cb and 'mov [0x1001fd94],eax' at 0x16e8. Each needs a jump to a code cave in the 0xF03 bytes of .text slack. The launcher, stage-fleetres and gameres keys must follow the new name. Nothing else exists: the share holds only demos, Turok 1 builds and dgVoodoo2, which does not run on XP.

titles.fix_risk: (1) Low, but it needs an agent release. (2) High: a hand-made patch to a DX6 renderer. The projection is probably fixed at 4:3, so 16:9 would stretch, and the menus and HUD at 1920 wide are untested. It is client-only, so multiplayer is unaffected. The edit keeps the file size, so publish through gvfs.
titles.hw_check: On an XP LCD box, first DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Turok2\Data\config.ned; after a GAMESYNC or GAMERES APPLY all six mode keys read 0. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Turok2" "Play Turok 2 - Multiplayer.bat"; DOWNLOAD config.ned again and 1024^x^768 now reads 1. In the game: OPTIONS > VIDEO (keyboard), then Properties. These are standard Win32 dialogs, so Tab, Alt+Down, arrows and UICLICK work. SCREENSHOT the Resolution combobox. Expected: 640 x 480, 800 x 600, 1024 x 768 and 1280 x 1024 only. Press Cancel. Close with taskkill /f /im "Turok2MPEnglish.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED on every point checked; not run on hardware, because the static evidence is conclusive. Added: .133 is also hit by the SEL43 zeroing. The 'no mode without the launcher' claim is supported by the .data initial values and by the scope of the 0x1000264d fallback. The survey's note on the impossible 1920x1080 DB rows is confirmed in the compat_render table.

titles.title: HiddenAndDangerous
titles.engine: Illusion Softworks / Lonely Cat Games, Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe v1.50 (2003 freeware). HDE.exe has PE timestamp 0x3f7d64c4 (2003-10-03). Direct3D 8 goes through igraph2.dll. The vendor config tool IConfig.exe has PE timestamp 0x3f788ef9 and loads d3d8.dll dynamically.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen, 32-bit. All three launchers write HKLM\Software\Lonely Cat Games\Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe\Config (Display width/height/bitdepth, Fullscreen) with FLEETRES -reg at every start, overriding install.reg's 800x600. GAMERES REG rules rewrite the same values at sync, after gs_merge_reg. REGREAD on .123, .145, .195 and .240 returns 1/1920/1080/32. Confirmed.
titles.menu_source: Enumerated from the driver. HDE.exe's Options > Video builder (0x462966) loops over the IGraph vtable. This review confirmed in igraph2.dll that +0xdc (0x10007320) is GetCreationParameters followed by IDirect3D8::GetAdapterModeCount, and +0xe0 (0x10007360) is EnumAdapterModes, unfiltered. HDE keeps modes with w>=512 and h>=384, removes duplicates keyed on (h<<16|w), sorts by area, and formats each as '%i x %i'. The entries go into an unbounded map, with no upper bound or aspect filter, so 1920 x 1080 is listed last. IConfig.exe fills its Resolution combobox the same way. Its thresholds are data: [0x4150c8]=512, [0x4150cc]=384, and bpp must be at least 16, not exactly 16. This result is static only. The in-game menu sits behind the profile screen, which needs a human once.
titles.evidence: Survey: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/static-hd-videomenu.txt; {123,145,195,240}/reg-HD-config.txt; dirlist-HiddenAndDangerous.json (no Savegame directory, so no profile). Review: the igraph2.dll vtable slot 0x1002c914 (+0xe0), with the previous slot (+0xdc) pointing to 0x10007320, which calls [ecx+0x24] and then [ecx+0x18]. IConfig.exe's EnumAdapterModes loop at 0x4011d9-0x40124c. README-FLEET.txt and the LAN status doc record the mouse-only profile screen.
titles.fix: None needed for the list. As a caveat, the per-launch HKLM rewrite means an in-game APPLY lasts one session; on the LCDs that is the same 1920x1080 anyway. The unattended blocker is the profile screen, which needs a human once. After that, stage Savegame\<name>.bin and add 'profile "<name>"' to the launchers, as README-FLEET says.
titles.fix_risk: n/a. On Windows 7 (.195), if UAC is on, the launcher's HKLM write is virtualised per user while GAMERES writes the real key. Both write the same 1920x1080, so there is no conflict today. Keep them identical.
titles.hw_check: A person at .145, .240 or .123 creates a profile once with the mouse. Then open Options > Video and SCREENSHOT the resolution list; expect '1920 x 1080' last, sorted by area. Do not press APPLY CHANGES. An unattended proxy for the same D3D8 source: LAUNCH C:\Games\HiddenAndDangerous\Bin\IConfig.exe, SCREENSHOT its Resolution combobox (Alt+Down) and expect 1920 x 1080. Leave with Cancel, then REGREAD the Config key to confirm it is unchanged.
titles.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED statically, with the igraph2 vtable slots verified as well. Correction: IConfig filters bpp >= 16, not 16 bpp only. Not exercised on hardware: the in-game menu is unreachable without a human-made profile, and the static chain is complete.

titles.title: AliensVsPredator
titles.engine: Rebellion's AvP engine, Gold Edition. avp.exe is 2,169,856 B, md5 91bb8e752f42d35f594fc06feabd49cf, PE timestamp 0x38d8cb5c (2000-03-22), subsystem 3.10, DirectDraw 6 / Direct3D. It is byte-identical to the avp.exe on the Gold disc 1 image. It imports no drive or volume APIs and has no insert-disc strings. The CD check lives only in the installer (setup.ins calls CDCheck.dll, CDCHECK_CDVERIFICATION).
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 at 16 bpp, and the game dies before its menu. The library deploys the tree, and 'Aliens vs Predator.lnk' is on all four LCD desktops, pointing straight at avp.exe with no FLEETRES and no GAMERES rule. No LCD box has AvP_Video.cfg, so the built-in default of 640x480x16 applies. Every last run (.123, .145, .195, .240) ends with Menus\IntroFont.rim not found, 'AwCreateGraphic(): ERROR: No data medium is specified', and 'ASSERTION FAILED! pSurface alt_tab.cpp 198'. No log contains a 'Loaded FastFile' line. Confirmed.
titles.menu_source: Driver-enumerated by the code, but never observed. The DirectDraw EnumDisplayModes callback (0x559344) keeps modes with bpp > 8, w >= 512, h >= 384 and a depth the D3D caps allow, and stops at 100. This review found the call at 0x559629 uses dwFlags=0, so refresh rates are not enumerated separately and the 100 cap cannot cut these boxes' lists of about 15-24 modes. By the code, 1920x1080 would be listed once the game starts. It has never reached its menu on this fleet.
titles.evidence: Review: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/review-ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/static-avp-installshield-deobfuscation.txt. All 201 files in the Gold-install MD5 list (github.com/atsb/NakedAVP README) match the staged tree: 56 as-is, and 145 after the InstallShield 5 de-obfuscation plain[i] = ror8(c[i]^0xD5, 2) - (i % 0x47), with a per-file seed of 0. By directory, avp_huds is 23 de-obfuscated, avp_rifs 63 de-obfuscated, and fastfile 55 as-is plus 59 de-obfuscated (58 Tex*.FFL and ffinfo.txt); language.txt matches as-is. A whole-tree magic scan adds 9 more obfuscated FMVs (8 .bik and IntroSound.smk; they decode to 'BIKf' and 'SMK2'), for 154 files. Gold disc 1 (/mnt/retro-share/Files/Games/Windows XP/Aliens vs Predator Gold (1999) - Disc 1.zip, MODE2/2352) carries these files obfuscated: TEX1.FFL at LBA 52969 is a Form-1 sector and its data starts 9cc8f4e8, identical to the staged file. The retail installer de-obfuscates them when it copies. Survey: ../ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/static-avp-data-check.txt and {123,145,195,240}/AliensVsPredator__LOGFILE.TXT.
titles.fix: The root cause is now CONFIRMED, not a lead. The staged tree is the raw disc payload with InstallShield file obfuscation still applied. The fix: de-obfuscate exactly those 154 files in the staged tree (fastfile/Tex1-58.FFL, fastfile/ffinfo.txt, avp_huds/*.rif, avp_rifs/*.rif, and the 9 FMVs), using the transform above. It reproduces the known-good Gold install byte for byte for every referenced file. Do NOT touch Snd*.FFL, common.ffl, *.dat, shape_rifs (REBINFF2) or anything else: those are already plain. No build-VM install is required, although running the retail installer in the VM would produce the same bytes and needs the disc mounted for its CDCheck.dll. Then purge and GAMESYNC per the staged-game loop, and confirm 'Loaded FastFile:' lines. For 1080p afterwards, either a per-box launcher writes AvP_Video.cfg (32 bytes: 16-byte DirectDraw device GUID, a flag, then w/h/bpp), or the in-game Options > Video list is used. Also correct PER-TITLE-STATUS ('not staged, CLOSED as BLOCKED'), README-FLEET ('byte-complete' was a size-only comparison) and the compat DB's 'runs, d3d 640x480' rows.
titles.fix_source: Already in tree. The transform is a six-line function applied to files already in /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/AliensVsPredator. The reference MD5s for verification come from the NakedAVP README (web). The disc image on the share is only needed for the VM-installer alternative.
titles.fix_risk: Low for the data: an exact reproduction of the installer's own transform, MD5-verified for 145 files, with the 9 FMVs verified by magic only. Every file keeps its size, so publish through gvfs (fresh mtime), verify each file through /mnt before the next, and do not use smbclient: a 2007 timestamp can defeat GAMESYNC's resume test. The whole-tree write is about 141 MB. How the engine handles a 16:9 aspect is still unevaluated, and a per-box AvP_Video.cfg writer is new work.
titles.hw_check: After the library fix, purge and GAMESYNC, then on .145/.240/.123 EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\AliensVsPredator" "avp.exe". Wait 30 s, taskkill /f /im "avp.exe", and DOWNLOAD C:\Games\AliensVsPredator\LOGFILE.TXT. It passes with 'Loaded FastFile:' lines and no 'ASSERTION FAILED'. Only then drive Options > Video with the keyboard; the DB lists AvP among the relative-mouse menus. GDI capture of AvP fullscreen is recorded as black (measured on .133), so read the result through LOGFILE, DISPLAYCFG get after choosing 1920x1080, or a person at the screen.
titles.verifier_notes: Major change. The survey's 'unverified lead' is proven and made exact: InstallShield 5 obfuscation, with all 201 reference MD5s reproduced. The survey's list missed 9 FMVs that are also obfuscated. The CD-check question is settled: avp.exe equals the disc exe and has no check; only the installer checks. Confirmed: the menu is unknown, the assertion on all four LCD boxes, and the corrections needed in PER-TITLE-STATUS and the DB. The game was not run on hardware in this review; the fix changes library data, which this phase does not do.
